column3: Nearly repeats the final-day settlement and adds each soul's self-defense.
Connects what is earned to accountable spending from good possessions.
Makes the return a certain gathering-day before the same full requital.
Applies full requital to concealed appropriation brought on the Resurrection Day.
Extends accountability to what souls disclose or conceal before God's judgment.
Adds graded outcomes alongside full payment for deeds without injustice.
Grounds each soul's earned requital in creation by truth.
Contrasts the fear of poverty with God's promise, without return or requital.
Frames daily death-like taking, return, and report of deeds.
Defines the feared day as one without substitution, intercession, or aid.
Shows charitable good fully returned without wronging the giver.
Places the return of all matters under God's ownership.
Reinforces the day when no soul can answer for another.
Commends wisdom and remembrance but adds no final-account detail.
Links wrongful association to what people kept earning.
States personal earning, no transferred burden, then return and disclosure.

Names the hereafter's reward for those who believe and are mindful.
Links every soul's death directly to return to God.

Links charity, hidden or open, to expiation and God's knowledge of deeds.

Makes spending on the needy known to God, supporting accountable charity.

Places financial conduct under God's command, return, and enduring consequence.

Sets divine erasure of usury against increase of charities.
Only names Abraham as one who fulfilled.
States origination, re-creation, and return to God.
Promises believing, prayerful givers reward with their Lord.
Recalls an earlier people as more unjust and transgressing.

Immediately situates mindfulness within abandoning remaining usury.

Commands mindfulness and forbids humiliation in a local scene.

Depicts people fearing a day of overturned hearts and eyes.

Sets an appointed return to God for judgment in disputed matters.
Identifies a wrongdoer people but adds no relevant account motif.
Uses the overwhelming day as a warning that calls for mindfulness.
Names God as worthy of mindfulness and forgiveness.

Makes God know secret, public, and acquired deeds.
Turns mindfulness into just, documented debt practice before the warning in 2:281.
Condemns fabrication and denial as wrongdoing without final-account detail.
Provides a concrete sign of death and revival under God's power.
Describes clear signs leading from darkness to light.
Couples ritual completion with mindfulness and severe punishment.
States that God did not wrong prior peoples; they wronged themselves.
Closely restates same-day earning-based recompense, no injustice, and swift account.
Explicitly denies divine wrongdoing and assigns wrongdoing to the people.
Shows every soul tested by what it sent ahead and returned to the true Master.
Addresses full measure-taking, only indirectly related to full requital.
States God repays every soul for what it earned and is swift in account.
Joins fulfilling covenant and mindfulness with God's love for the mindful.
Restates full payment for every soul's deeds under complete divine knowledge.
States God's knowledge of every soul's earning and the final outcome.
Makes mindfulness include examining what each soul sent ahead for tomorrow.
Names Hell as recompense for what was earned in a specific case.
Links a soul's forfeiture to earning and excludes ransom or intercession.
Names the blessed state of the mindful without account mechanics.
Portrays God as standing over every soul for what it earned.

Sets return to God and report of deeds within divine comprehensive knowledge.
Uses fear of returned oaths in a testimony procedure.
Connects Resurrection punishment with tasting what was earned.
Rebukes the false assumption of not being returned to God.
States life, death, and certain gathering for the Resurrection Day.
Denies an idol's ability to answer, harm, or benefit.
Joins death with full payment of wages on the Resurrection Day and final outcomes.
Shows wrongdoers disputing before their Lord, without the settlement formula.
Applies mindfulness and self-wronging to divorce limits.
Affirms God's judgment, praise in the hereafter, and return to Him.

Contrasts mercy with the wrongdoers' lack of protector or helper.
Shows people recognizing themselves as wrongdoers.
Frames worship by the Creator in light of return to Him.
Says the people wronged themselves after provision, not God.
Describes incapacitation with no final-account contribution.

Contrasts entry into mercy with prepared painful punishment.
Depicts the comprehensive record, deeds found present, and no wrong by the Lord.
Says prior earnings did not avail their possessors.
Records denial and uncertainty about the certain Hour.
Uses stars for guidance, unrelated to final return and requital.
Relates change and unavoidable divine decree, not the final settlement.

Shows promise fulfilled, rescue, and destruction of excess.

Links what people have earned with God's swift reckoning.
Shows every soul finding its good and evil deeds present on that day.

Affirms the certain gathering on the Resurrection Day.
Makes sin-acquisition fall upon the one who acquired it.
States that whoever does evil will be requited for it.
Promises no injustice, even the smallest amount, to righteous believers.
Promises full payment of rewards and additional favor for believers.
Promises forgiveness and great reward to believers who do righteous deeds.

Makes the true weighing decisive on that day.
Links light scales to loss of self through wronging the signs.
Makes the recompense match what people had been doing.
Denies divine injustice toward servants while assigning consequence to prior deeds.
Counts every hardship and effort as a righteous deed recorded for recompense.

Connects evil deeds to matching recompense and disgrace.

Makes wrongdoers taste the enduring punishment for their earnings.
Promises full payment in this life for those seeking only its adornment.
States that the Lord will fully pay all people for their deeds.
Shows the wrongdoers' futile ransom attempt and their evil account.
Contrasts conveying the message with God's taking of the account.
Defers rather than neglects wrongdoers until a fearsome day.

Makes every person's deed fastened to them and brought as an opened record.
Makes the person read their record and suffice as their own accountant.

Places punishment before return to the Lord for a further punishment.
Links faith and righteous work to the finest reward after the return frame.

Joins creation from earth, return to it, and emergence from it again.
Announces that people's account has drawn near.
Sets just scales for the Resurrection Day and denies any injustice, even a mustard seed.

Places the final judgment among communities on the Resurrection Day with God.
Sets a truthful record that speaks against people without wronging them.
Makes tongues, hands, and feet testify about what they used to do.
States that God will pay their true due in full on that day.
Makes the recompense for evil match what people used to do.
Promises better for good and only like-for-like recompense for evil.
Connects additional burdens on the Resurrection Day to misleading others.
Declares that even a mustard seed will be brought forth by God.
Reserves an unseen reward for deeds previously done.
Affirms a comprehensive record and recompense for believers' righteous deeds.
Denies mutual injustice on that day and limits recompense to one's deeds.
Denies transferred burdens and makes self-purification benefit its doer.
States no soul is wronged that day and each is repaid only for its deeds.
Limits recompense to what people used to do.
Shows wrongdoers offering all earth's wealth and more as futile ransom on the Resurrection Day.
Makes righteous action benefit oneself and evil fall upon oneself, denying divine injustice.
Sets evil recompense as its equivalent while opening forgiveness and reconciliation.
Makes every person held in pledge for what they earned.
States that God recompenses evildoers for their deeds and rewards those who do good.
States that no bearer bears another's burden.
Limits a person to what they have striven for.
Makes a person's striving visible.
Promises the fullest recompense for that striving.
Makes God resurrect all and inform them of deeds He counted though they forgot them.
Affirms resurrection, report of deeds, and divine power over all things.
Names the gathering day as the day of mutual loss and gain, with deeds expiated for believers.
Depicts the day of presentation when no secret is hidden.
Makes each person informed that day of what they sent ahead and left behind.
Warns of the near punishment when a person sees what their hands sent ahead.
Makes a person remember what they strove for when the great event comes.
States that every soul will know what it brought forth.
Makes every soul know what it sent ahead and left behind.
Challenges those who defraud the measure with their coming resurrection.
Names that resurrection as a tremendous day.
Depicts people standing before the Lord of the worlds on that day.
Introduces receiving one's record in the right hand.
Promises an easy account to the recipient of the right-hand record.
Shows that recipient returning joyfully to their people.
Introduces receiving one's record from behind the back.
Links that record to calling for destruction.
Links that record to entering the blaze.
Shows people emerging separately to be shown their deeds.
Makes even an atom's weight of good visible.
Makes even an atom's weight of evil visible.
Sets heavy scales as the measure of a favorable outcome.
Links heavy scales to a contented life.
Sets light scales as the contrary measure.
Links light scales to the abyss.
Asks what makes that abyss known.
Names it a fiercely hot fire.
Foretells questioning about blessing on that day.
